bindings.label: Patient had painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis for 1 month

Patient is a 78-year-old man; medical history includes elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior, and four years after initial presentation he experienced fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite

Current illness began 1 month prior to admission with asymptomatic green-yellow welts and swelling of the glans penis; the swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an orange over 4 days
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement

Physical examination showed grossly edematous glans penis and corona, with a 3.7 x 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue; no urethral discharge was present
Penile biopsy shows atypical B-cell infiltrate (CD20+, CD79a+, CD5+) with clonal IgH rearrangement
PET-CT shows FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes
Systemic B-cell lymphoma involving the penis
Penile biopsy shows no evidence of primary penile malignancy
Penile biopsy shows no evidence of infectious/inflammatory ulcer
